_comment: Known circular imports, READ AND CLASSIFIED — never exempt. Only shrinks: a cycle that leaves
the tree must leave this file in the same commit, and check-import-cycles.mjs fails if it does
not. A cycle NOT listed here fails immediately.
Measured 2026-08-19 on the first run of the ported check: 17 distinct cycles, four families.
Burned down 2026-08-23: 16 fixed, 1 left. What remains is entry 9 below — families A, B and C
are gone. The fix in every case was the same move: put the shared declaration in its own module
beside the pair, and point BOTH sides at it. No re-export was left behind on any parent, because
a re-export restores the cycle for whoever uses it.
⚠ TWO OF THE FOUR FAMILY CLASSIFICATIONS ABOVE WERE WRONG, AND BOTH WERE WRONG IN THE SAME
DIRECTION — they called a VALUE import type-only. Recorded because the error is instructive, not
because it was expensive:
- Family B's stated fix was 'extract the rule-facing types into lib/rules/types.ts so rules
depend on the contract rather than on the engine'. That file ALREADY EXISTED and the four
cycles were still live, which is the tell. The real edge was `hasBeenActionedFor`, a
FUNCTION the four rules import from the engine, and no amount of type extraction touches it.
Fixed by moving that helper to lib/rules/actioned.ts. Had the stated fix been applied on
faith, it would have produced a green-looking commit that fixed nothing.
- Family A's entry 11 (DepositDamageSection) was called type-only too. It imports
CLASSIFICATION_LABELS, a value, and was a genuine runtime loop that worked only on module
initialisation order — the same hazard the check exists for, sitting inside the family
described as harmless.
The lesson is not 'the classifier was careless'. It is that 'type-only' is a claim about every
import specifier on the edge, and reading the first one is not reading them.
FAMILY D — auth/tier, and the ONE that is not type-only (1 of 17). STILL OPEN.
`lib/tier/getOrgTier` imports the VALUE `getServerOrgMembership` from `lib/auth/server`,
which reaches back through `can` -> `orgRoles` -> `getOrgTier`. A real runtime loop on the
authorisation path: it works today only because of the order Node happens to initialise these
modules in. Highest priority of the four, and the reason this check is worth its sixty lines.
Deliberately NOT bundled into the 2026-08-23 burn-down: the other sixteen were declaration
moves with no behavioural surface, and this one is a restructure of the authorisation path.
It wants its own change, its own walk, and a decision about WHERE the tier lookup belongs —
not a fix appended to a mechanical sweep.
Entry 1 below.
